turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Doctor, over the past year my shortness of breath has been steadily getting worse, and I’ve also lost weight. I don’t have fevers, cough, or chest pain.”

Do you smoke, or have you had significant exposure to dusts, chemicals, birds, mold, or asbestos?
Do you smoke, or have you had significant exposure to dusts, chemicals, birds, mold, or asbestos?

“Yes, I’m an active smoker—about 36 pack-years. I also worked in a steel mill in high school and did construction work, but I don’t recall specific asbestos or heavy dust/chemical exposures beyond that.”
How old are you, and have you noticed wheezing or coughing up any blood?
“Doctor, I’m 56 years old. I haven’t noticed wheezing, and I haven’t coughed up any blood. My main issue has been steadily worsening shortness of breath along with weight loss.”
Do you get short of breath mainly with exertion, and have you had any leg swelling, trouble breathing when lying flat, or waking up short of breath at night?
“Doctor, it’s mainly with exertion, like walking or climbing stairs. I haven’t noticed leg swelling, I can breathe okay lying flat, and I’m not waking up short of breath at night.”
Have you had any chest imaging or breathing tests, and if so, what did they show?
“Doctor, I haven’t had any chest imaging or breathing tests yet—no X-rays, CT scans, or spirometry—so far.”
Any history of tuberculosis exposure, night sweats, or swollen lymph nodes?

“Doctor, I don’t recall any tuberculosis exposure, and I haven’t had night sweats or swollen lymph nodes. I’ve mainly just had steadily worsening shortness of breath with weight loss over the past year.”

[ABSTAIN] Insufficient evidence without exam, imaging, or spirometry to confidently narrow the cause of chronic progressive dyspnea and weight loss.
[POSSIBLE] lung cancer, COPD/emphysema, interstitial lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, chronic heart failure
